content: Standard robust-statistics guidance: a trimmed mean removes a fixed top/bottom percentage (typically 10-20% per tail) before averaging; this is well-defined for larger samples but degenerate/undefined for the n=3-10 sample sizes typical of a single character's keystroke count in one exercise (trimming 20% of 3 samples removes ~0.6 of a sample, not a whole one). Median is the standard robust alternative for small-n samples since it needs no percentage-based trim and is far less sensitive to a single remaining outlier than a mean. Recommended shape for keebdrill: treat the >1000ms/<25ms gap discard as the 'trim' step (an absolute-threshold trim, not a percentage trim), then take the median (not a further trimmed mean) of whatever samples remain -- this matches typing-analytics tools like keybr.com's median-per-key-latency convention.
